headline_marked: [[Bijoya Dashami today]] as religious rituals mark end of Durga Puja across Bangladesh
headline: Bijoya Dashami today as religious rituals mark end of Durga Puja across Bangladesh
summary: Hindu devotees across Bangladesh are observing Bijoya Dashami, the final day of the five-day Sharadiya Durga Puja, with special prayers and rituals before idol immersion.
details: Today marks the auspicious Bijoya Dashami, the final day of the Sharadiya Durga Puja. Religious rituals and ceremonies are actively underway in various puja mandaps across Bangladesh since morning.

The grand five-day festival for the Hindu community will conclude with the immersion of Durga idols in designated water bodies on Wednesday, October 21. The atmosphere in mandaps is filled with the sounds of farewell.
Devotees of all ages are participating in the worship of the Goddess, offering 'anjali' and prayers. Following the puja, 'prasad' is being distributed in many mandaps.
During the Dashami puja, offerings such as 'jora', 'pan', and 'shapla dala' are presented to the idol. After the formal rituals, devotees engage in 'Sindoor Khela', a joyous tradition.

Beyond religious observances, many are spending the festive day meeting relatives and acquaintances, exchanging greetings, and enjoying time together. All religious ceremonies will culminate with the immersion of the idols.

headline_marked: [[54 Bangladeshis die in Russia-Ukraine war]] after going for jobs, many more missing
headline: 54 Bangladeshis die in Russia-Ukraine war after going for jobs, many more missing
summary: Many were allegedly lured to Russia with promises of good jobs but were instead sent to the front lines of the Ukraine war. Families face challenges in confirming deaths and retrieving bodies.
details: At least 54 Bangladeshis have reportedly died over the past three years after traveling to Russia for promised jobs, only to be sent to the front lines of the Ukraine war. Many were allegedly deceived by recruiting agencies, finding themselves in combat zones instead of the high-paying positions they sought.

Abdullah Al Mamun from Lalmonirhat is one such victim. He called his younger brother a day before being sent to war, saying they might not meet again. Five months later, his family, burdened by debt, remains uncertain of his death as no body has been recovered.

Mamun was part of a group of 30 Bangladeshis who went to Russia on May 7. After 21 days of training, they were divided into groups of 16, 8, and 6 and sent to war. Two individuals, Adnan Hossain and Rajon Hossain, managed to escape after being injured and confirmed the deaths of others.

According to Adnan, Russia does not disclose information about Bangladeshi deaths in the war or repatriate bodies, often listing them as 'missing.' Bangladesh's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is in regular diplomatic discussions with Russia, which has so far reported information on 40 missing or deceased Bangladeshis.

The Bangladeshi Embassy in Russia has raised objections regarding recruiting agencies sending workers without proper verification. A letter from the embassy to the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare stated that some agencies sent workers under different names after the embassy refused to authenticate their requests.

Bangladesh's Ambassador to Russia, Md. Nazrul Islam, stated that over 90% of workers voluntarily joined the war, with Russia possessing written proof. He also noted that Russian authorities are not handing over bodies. Claiming compensation for deceased or missing individuals is a complex process requiring heirs to stay in Russia for at least six months.

Fortify Rights and Truth Hounds reported in March that 34 out of over a hundred Bangladeshi youths fighting for Russia in Ukraine had died. The Special Response Battalion (SRB) also confirmed receiving information about at least 20 deaths among 30 Bangladeshis sent to war in June.
